source_prompt_excerpt: EXPLORE & REASON. Consider the following graph of the function y=x+2. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] A. What is the domain? B. Sketch a function that resembles the graph, but restrict its domain to exclude 2. Sample Student Work: [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]
notes: Two-panel figure, one per placeholder. Panel A plots the given y=x+2 line with x- and y-intercepts marked. Panel B renders the 'sample student work' answer described directly in the prompt text ('resembles the graph, but restrict its domain to exclude 2') as the same line with an open-circle hole at (2,4). No data invented -- the hole location is the line's own value at x=2, taken from the text's own instruction, not a separate fabricated curve. Point label on panel A needed one reposition (was colliding with the '-2' axis tick number); fixed by anchoring the label above the axis instead of at the tick.

source_prompt_excerpt: Identify an Extraneous Solution... graph f(x) = (1)/(x-5) + (x)/(x-3) and g(x) = (2)/(x^2-8x+15). [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] Both graphs have vertical asymptotes at x = 3 and x = 5... graphs only intersect in one point, at x = -1.
notes: Both rational functions plotted with domain split around the two named vertical asymptotes (x=3, x=5, drawn as dashed reference lines) and restrict-y-to-domain clipping so the asymptotic blow-up stays inside a readable window. Marked the stated intersection point (-1, 1/12), computed directly from the two given formulas (not fabricated).

source_prompt_excerpt: Find All Real nth Roots... consider the function f(x)=x^3-125. The zeroes of f are the cube roots of 125. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] The graph of f has only one x-intercept. Therefore, 5 is the only real cube root of 125.
notes: None. Single cubic f(x)=x^3-125 plotted over a window showing its one real zero at x=5 (marked). Compiled clean on first attempt.

source_prompt_excerpt: Use nth Roots to Solve Equations. Solve 2x^5=64... x=2 [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] one point of intersection... Solve 3x^4=1875... x=+-5 [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] The graphs show 2 points of intersection.
notes: Two-panel figure, one per placeholder. Panel A: y=x^5 vs. the horizontal line y=32, single intersection at (2,32) matching the algebra. Panel B: y=x^4 vs. y=625, two intersections at (-5,625) and (5,625). All curves and marked points are named/derived directly from the worked algebra in the prompt, not invented.

source_prompt_excerpt: EXPLORE & REASON. The graph shows y = x^2. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] A. Find all possible values of x or y so that the point is on the graph... C. Draw a graph of y = x^3. Use the graph to approximate each value.
notes: Only one [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] placeholder appears in this variant of the item (before part A), so only y=x^2 was rendered -- part C's 'draw a graph of y=x^3' is a student-drawing instruction here, not a supplied figure slot (contrast with the '-2' duplicate item below, which does carry a second placeholder for it). No points marked on the parabola: part A asks students to find those exact coordinate values themselves, so marking them would leak the answer (project convention: no answer leaks in student-facing prompts/figures).

source_prompt_excerpt: EXPLORE & REASON. The graph shows y=x^2. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]... C. Draw a graph of y=x^3. Use the graph to approximate each value. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]
notes: This variant carries two placeholders (y=x^2 before part A, y=x^3 before part C), so both panels were rendered. Neither curve has points marked, consistent with the no-answer-leak convention -- parts A and C ask students to read approximate values off the unmarked graphs themselves.

source_prompt_excerpt: Additional Example 6. A clerk is wrapping two cube-shaped packages... The edge length of the larger package is 3 in. greater... surface area of the larger package is 384 in.^2... [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] 384=6(x+3)^2...
notes: HELD -- no coordinate function, table, or point set is named anywhere in this item for a graph. The algebra solves 384=6(x+3)^2 for a real-world cube-wrapping word problem; the original [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] most plausibly held a diagram/photo of the two physical wrapped packages, not a coordinate-plane curve, and the text gives nothing plottable (no function of x and y, no table of values). Per the 'fabricate no data' instruction, no .tex was written for this id.

source_prompt_excerpt: Identify an Extraneous Solution. Solve sqrt(3x-2)=x-4... x=9 or x=2... Graph on one grid, y=sqrt(3x-2) and y=x-4. Then graph on another grid y=3x-2 and y=(x-4)^2. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]
notes: Two-panel figure per the two explicitly requested grids. Panel 1: y=sqrt(3x-2) and y=x-4, intersecting only at (9,5) as the text states (x=2 is algebraically excluded here since sqrt is nonnegative but x-4=-2 at x=2). Panel 2: y=3x-2 and y=(x-4)^2, intersecting at both (2,4) and (9,25) -- matching the text's claim that squaring introduced the extra intersection at x=2. Both intersection sets verified by direct substitution, not assumed.

source_prompt_excerpt: Solve an Equation With Two Radicals. Solve sqrt(x+9)-sqrt(2x)=3... x=0 or x=72... the only solution is 0... graphing y=sqrt(x+9)-sqrt(2x) and y=3 together. They intersect only at x=0. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]
notes: None. Plotted the named curve and horizontal line over a window showing the curve decreasing away from its sole intersection with y=3 at (0,3), matching the text. Compiled clean on first attempt.

source_prompt_excerpt: Solving Radical Equations table. Step 1 Isolate the radical: 2sqrt(x+3)=x [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]. Step 3 Solve: x=6 or x=-2. Step 4 Eliminate extraneous solutions: 2sqrt(9)-6=0 (6=6, valid); 2sqrt(1)-(-2)=0 (2 != -2, extraneous).
notes: Plotted y=2sqrt(x+3) and y=x, marking the valid solution (6,6) and the curve's actual value at x=-2 -- (-2,2), labeled 'extraneous' -- to visually show it does not lie on y=x (2 != -2), exactly matching the Step 4 check shown in the table. Both this id and the '-2' duplicate share identical content since the registry carries the same GRAPH table cell twice.

source_prompt_excerpt: Solving Radical Equations table (alternate layout, GRAPH cell in Step 3 row). Step 1: 2sqrt(x+3)=x. Step 3: x=6 or x=-2. Step 4: 2sqrt(9)=6 (valid, 6=6); 2sqrt(1)=-2 (2 != -2, extraneous). [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]
notes: Duplicate registry row of 5-4-savvas-concept-summary-lesson-5-4 (same table, GRAPH cell just placed at a different row in this layout variant). Identical figure content: y=2sqrt(x+3) and y=x with (6,6) marked valid and (-2,2) marked extraneous.

source_prompt_excerpt: Higher Order Thinking Use the graph of y=3^x to estimate the value of log_3 50. Explain your reasoning. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]
notes: Plotted y=3^x with a dashed y=50 reference line (the target value named in the question) but deliberately did NOT mark the intersection point or its x-coordinate -- marking it would hand the student the estimate the exercise asks them to make themselves from the graph.

source_prompt_excerpt: Inverses of Exponential and Logarithmic Functions. A. f(x)=10^(x+1)... f^-1(x)=log x - 1 [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] B. g(x)=log_7(x+5)... g^-1(x)=7^x-5 [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]
notes: Two-panel figure, one per part. Each panel shows the named function, its algebraically-derived inverse (both given in the worked solution text), and the y=x reflection line; panel B also marks the vertical asymptote at x=-5 from g's domain. Needed two follow-up legend-position fixes after the initial visual check: south-east (first attempt) overlapped the x-axis tick labels in panel A; north-west (second attempt) then overlapped the rising blue curve; final placement, north-east inside the axis, is the one region neither curve reaches. No data changed at any point.

source_prompt_excerpt: Logarithmic Functions table. GRAPH: [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] The functions are inverses so their graphs are reflections of each other across the line y=x. EQUATIONS: y=log x | y=10^x.
notes: Standard log/exponential inverse pair (base 10) with y=x reflection line and marked (1,0)/(0,1) reference points, following the same house style as the existing pilot's 6-4-ex-1/6-4-ex-2 (base 2 case). Compiled clean on first attempt.

source_prompt_excerpt: CONCEPT SUMMARY Logarithmic Functions. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] The functions are inverses so their graphs are reflections of each other across the line with equation y=x. TABLE: y=log x | y=10^x ...
notes: Duplicate registry row of 6-4-savvas-concept-summary-lesson-6-4 (same content, alternate layout). Identical figure: y=log x, y=10^x, y=x reflection line, (1,0)/(0,1) marked.

source_prompt_excerpt: Graph each function and identify the domain and range. List any intercepts or asymptotes. Describe the end behavior. y=log_5 x.
notes: None. Single log_5 x curve; vertical asymptote is the y-axis itself (already drawn by axis lines=middle, so no extra dashed line needed); x-intercept (1,0) marked.

source_prompt_excerpt: Graph each function and identify the domain and range. List any intercepts or asymptotes. Describe the end behavior. y=log_8 x.
notes: None. Same treatment as q14, base 8.

source_prompt_excerpt: Graph each function and identify the domain and range. List any intercepts or asymptotes. Describe the end behavior. y=log_{(3)/(10)}x.
notes: Base 3/10 < 1, so the function is decreasing (rendered as ln(x)/ln(0.3)); x-intercept (1,0) marked.

source_prompt_excerpt: Graph each function and identify the domain and range. List any intercepts or asymptotes. Describe the end behavior. y=log_{0.1}x.
notes: Base 0.1 < 1, decreasing log (rendered as ln(x)/ln(0.1)); x-intercept (1,0) marked.

source_prompt_excerpt: Model with Mathematics r=90-25log(t+1)... Make a table of values... sketch the graph... TABLE: t=9,99,200,300,400 -> r=65,40,32.5,28,24.9 [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]
notes: Plotted the named function and verified it reproduces every answer-key table value to the stated rounding (t=9 -> r=65.0, t=99 -> 40.0, t=200 -> 32.4 (table rounds 32.5), t=300 -> 28.0, t=400 -> 24.9); all five points marked and labeled exactly as given, no values altered.

source_prompt_excerpt: SAT/ACT The graph shows the exponential function f(x) = 5^{x+1}. Which of the following functions represents its inverse, f^-1(x)? [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] (A)(B)(C)(D) answer choices...
notes: Plotted f(x)=5^(x+1) with its y-intercept (0,5) and one additional computed point (-1,1) marked. The four multiple-choice answer options are a text table, not part of the figure, so they were left out of the .tex.

source_prompt_excerpt: Sketch the functions represented by the tables... A. x=10^-10,0.01,1,2,10 -> g(x)=-8,0,2,2.301,3. B. x=-1,0,1,2,3,4 -> h(x)=0.001,0.01,0.1,1,10,100. Answer: g(x) is the logarithmic function; yes, inverses. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]
notes: Reverse-engineered the exact closed forms from the two given tables: h(x)=10^(x-2) fits all six h-table rows exactly, and g(x)=log(x)+2 fits all five g-table rows exactly -- confirming they are inverses, matching the answer key. Marked every table point on its curve. Two of the most extreme table points (g(10^-10)=-8, hugging the vertical asymptote, and h(4)=100, ~10x taller than the rest of the visible range) fall outside a window that would still be readable for the other 9 points, so those two were called out with text annotations instead of plotted off-scale markers; no point was altered or dropped from the data itself, only its on-page placement.

source_prompt_excerpt: ADDITIONAL EXAMPLE 2. Graph the function f(x)=-log(x+3)-4... vertical asymptote translated 3 units left... reflected over the x-axis... translated 4 units down. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]
notes: Plotted f(x)=-log(x+3)-4 plus the parent y=log x (named explicitly in the 'compared to the graph of y=log x' sentence) for reference, with the translated vertical asymptote at x=-3 drawn dashed and one computed key point (-2,-4) marked (f(-2) = -log(1)-4 = -4).

source_prompt_excerpt: EXPLORE & REASON. Look at the graph of y = log x and the ordered pairs shown. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] A. Complete the table shown. x: 3 | 5 | 15. log x: ___
notes: Plotted y=log x and marked the three points at x=3, 5, 15 that the prompt says are 'shown' on the original graph -- the exercise has students transcribe already-displayed values into a table, so marking these reproduces the given figure rather than leaking a derived answer. Point labels kept symbolic ($\log 3$ etc., not the decimal), and no y-axis tick sits at those exact heights, so the precise decimal still has to be read off the marked point rather than an added gridline.

source_prompt_excerpt: EXPLORE AND REASON. Look at the graph of y=log x and the ordered pairs shown. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure] A. Complete the table shown. x | 3 | 5 | 15. log x
notes: Duplicate registry row of 6-5-savvas-model-discuss-lesson-6-5-launch (same content, alternate capitalization/layout). Identical figure.

source_prompt_excerpt: Higher Order Thinking The graph of y=log(1/x) and y=-log x are shown. Notice the graph is the same for both equations. Use properties of logarithms to explain why the graphs are the same. [GRAPH/TIKZ figure]
notes: Plotted both named functions as overlapping curves (solid blue underneath, red dashed on top) to visually demonstrate they coincide exactly, as the prompt states (log(1/x) = -log x algebraically).
